prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application first-viewport design comp, 1440×1000 target canvas
Primary request: Design a polished route-first homepage comp for TravelCanvas, a China domestic travel planning product whose brand voice is convenient and efficient. This is a real product UI mockup, not a poster.
Input images: Image 1 is a style-only reference. Inherit only its tea-mountain green and warm-paper palette, Chinese typography character, restrained border radii, and precise component feel. Do not copy its layout, page structure, content hierarchy, or long-form fields.
Scene/backdrop: A full desktop application viewport with no conventional top navigation. The interface itself fills the canvas.
Composition/framing: 1440×1000 landscape desktop viewport. Use an asymmetric split: a compact left planning panel taking about one third of the width and a spacious right route-map canvas taking about two thirds. Keep all important UI inside the first viewport with realistic margins and crisp alignment.
Left panel: At the upper left, a compact TravelCanvas wordmark. Below it, a confident large Chinese headline exactly “从想去，到走得通” and a concise supporting sentence that emphasizes a fast, workable trip-planning flow. Show only the essential start fields: destination set to “杭州”; a date field with a simple calendar icon; compact segmented or stepper controls showing “2天” and “2人”; one strong primary CTA exactly “开始发现地点”. Below the CTA, provide a clear next-layer collapsed area with three understated disclosure rows or chips labeled exactly “预算”, “偏好”, and “餐饮”, signaling optional details without exposing full forms. The panel should feel fast and frictionless, not like an enterprise dashboard.
Right panel: A light, stylized but product-realistic Hangzhou route map canvas using subtle warm-paper streets, pale water shapes for West Lake, delicate neighborhood lines, and minimal geographic labeling. Place only a few real example destinations: “西湖”, “灵隐寺”, and “湖滨餐厅”. Connect them with an elegant tea-green route line and small numbered route pins, with one terracotta-orange emphasis point. Include a lightly elevated floating place summary card on the map, with restrained details such as place name, route order, and a short neutral status; do not invent reviews, ratings, prices, opening hours, or unverifiable claims. Add a small unobtrusive source / query-time style line to suggest trustworthy data, without dominating the design.
Style/medium: premium high-fidelity SaaS/product UI screenshot; modern Chinese travel product; precise, professional, efficient; subtle editorial warmth; slightly rounded controls; exceptionally clean grid; restrained soft shadows only for the floating map card and active controls. Sharp legible interface text.
Color palette: tea-mountain green #226054 as primary; terracotta orange #df7255 as accent; warm sand #f6f4ee background; rice paper #fffdf8 surfaces; pine ink #18322e primary text. Supporting tints may only be quiet mixtures derived from these colors.
Typography: modern Chinese sans-serif for product UI, with a slightly editorial yet highly readable display treatment for the headline. Maintain a clear hierarchy and generous but efficient spacing.
Text (verbatim): “TravelCanvas”; “从想去，到走得通”; “杭州”; “2天”; “2人”; “开始发现地点”; “预算”; “偏好”; “餐饮”; “西湖”; “灵隐寺”; “湖滨餐厅”.
Constraints: no conventional navigation bar; no sidebar menu; no long form; no metric dashboard; no real photos; no fake review count, rating, price, hotel inventory, or promotional claim; no browser chrome; no device frame; no watermark. The map must read as a route-planning workspace rather than a decorative illustration. Preserve Chinese text accurately and keep interface elements usable and plausible.
Avoid: enterprise admin dashboard aesthetics, KPI cards, dense tables, purple or blue gradients, glassmorphism, neon glow, excessive shadows, excessive pills, giant empty hero space, tourism poster styling, cartoon illustration, photorealistic imagery, clutter, fake map-provider branding.
